name: English Opening
blurb: White starts with the c-pawn and fights for d5 from the side. A flexible, positional opening that often plays like a Sicilian with the colours reversed.

ideas.c4: Controls d5 from the side and keeps White's other centre pawns flexible.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3: Adds a second attacker to d5 and develops. This is like a Sicilian with the colours reversed and an extra move for White.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3: Prepares Bg2, putting the bishop on the long diagonal from h1 to a8.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2: The bishop now covers d5 and hits the c6 knight down the long diagonal.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6 e4: With pawns on c4 and e4, White has a firm grip on d5. This is the Botvinnik setup.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3: Develops with an attack on the e5 pawn.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e4 Ng5: The knight hits the advanced e4 pawn, and Black has to spend time holding it.
ideas.c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 g3: Prepares Bg2, the standard English bishop placement aiming at the centre.
ideas.c4 e6 Nf3: Against ...e6, White develops and waits. Pushing d4 would turn the game into a Queen's Gambit; the knight keeps that choice open.
ideas.c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3: White fianchettoes and will put pressure on d5 from a distance, as in the Catalan.
ideas.c4 c5 Nc3: Against the Symmetrical English, White develops toward d5 and keeps the same flexible setup.
ideas.c4 Nf6 Nf3: Develops and keeps every option open, waiting to see Black's setup before committing the centre pawns.
